content:
Adam Topaz said:

  1. We will release autoformalized artifacts that embody the standards this project promotes, demonstrating in practice what responsible autoformalization at scale looks like while providing material that researchers can readily build on.

Will "autoformalized artifacts" here include any of those things that result from human formalization projects, and should result from a good autoformalizer, but that don't naturally go in the same repository as the autoformalized proof? For example, mathlib branches ready to submit as PRs with all the many small API additions to existing parts of mathlib that any significant human formalization project yields (and a good autoformalizer ought to yield) whether or not the main content of that project is intended to end up in mathlib (an autoformalizer should not just put a Mathlib folder in its output to distinguish those pieces from the main content of its formalization, but should also do most of the work of preparing the PRs).

If you lead an autoformalization project, reach out about adopting the specification in your work.

I am interested in writing more Lean companions to undergraduate (and eventually graduate) math textbooks in the style of https://github.com/teorth/analysis and currently writing one for Axler's Linear Algebra https://github.com/rkirov/linear-algebra-done-right-lean. I am heavily using AI to produce a draft, and then manually editing and cleaning the text (see https://github.com/rkirov/linear-algebra-done-right-lean#status). I would be interested to align this type of work with the autoformalization spec where possible, even though this is not research of frontier-level work. I would like to use the spec to be able to more authoritatively say "AI was used, but this is not slop" to a potential reader who wants to do the exercises.

Separately, I am curious if as part of this initiative you are thinking of community building platform like https://www.erdosproblems.com/ or https://www.problemsilike.com/ centered around autoformalization. I believe there is a great number of math hobbyists that will be willing to donate tokens and general software engineering work to the autoformalization effort without fully understanding all the math that is being formalized. My thesis (I could be wrong here) is that energy is useful and can be put to good use advancing the broader goals of the formalization efforts, but a lot of it wasted right now (see daily posts on zulip about "I autoformalized something".) A single known platform centered around the canonical DAG of all math concepts and showing the current formalization frontier can be a coordination hub for hobbyists and math experts. In aggregate they will have all the necessary skills for a higher quality autoformalizations (with a path towards mathlib) without waste. Forming these working groups over zulip is currently hard, as it is not structured around the formalization goals directly. Projects-sized workflows for this exist in FLT and PNT+, but maybe a more central effort across all fields would be more efficient.

@Joseph Myers -- The precise shape of the autoformalized artifacts we will release is in flux, and will be informed by the experiments going on now, and those that will happen over the next six months. Also, Mathlib's policy for AI contributions is evolving, and we will always be aligned with that. One thing I think we should make clear is that the Formal Frontier project will never do anything to overwhelm Mathlib's review throughput. More generally, I think that whether or not AI is able to reliably produce mathlib quality autoformalized code is still an open question (we hope to answer this question in our project!).

Are there any artifacts now that give some idea of what is acceptable? I would like to have an idea before submitting the results of my experiments. In particular, amount/quality of comment lines, length of proofs of helper lemmas, particular stylistic issues involving simp and have and other Lean idioms, knowing bounds for these and other details would help.

Or do you need some seed material and I should just go ahead and submit my (AI-generated) Lean files that I would find acceptable (in my current state of ignorance)?
sender_full_name: J. J. Issai (project started by GRP)

content: I don't know what the autoformalization specification from Formal Frontier will be like, but #general > The role of AI companies in large formalisation projects has extensive discussion of what the community thinks is desirable from autoformalizations, both in terms of content and in terms of process / community interaction, so hopefully it will build on themes and ideas from that discussion.

@J. J. Issai (project started by GRP) the plan is to release a first version of this formalization spec in the near future. See https://mathlib-initiative.org/formal-frontier/ for some of the things it will cover.
We don't have any examples right now.
@Joseph Myers We are very much aware of that discussion, and participated in it. We absolutely are building on it.
